topic: Exact second-order minimax excess-risk frontier for a linear causal functional in a sequential (non-anticipating) experiment, over the unrestricted estimator class

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the constant-sharp minimax cumulative Neyman-regret value for adaptive two-arm ATE estimation, including an adaptive design attaining the local curvature-information frontier.

source_refs.excerpt: The ONLY open object (OEQ) is the constant-sharp minimax value: a matching constant-sharp UPPER bound.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked run establishes the logarithmic rate and a closed-form lower-side curvature-information complexity, but no adaptive allocation rule is proved to attain that complexity with the same universal leading constant. Existing tracking designs control cumulative variance inefficiency only up to non-sharp constants, clipping terms, or logarithmic-envelope slack; this is adjacent to the present excess-MSE frontier because both charge for learning an unknown Neyman allocation, but the regret and terminal-risk criteria are not interchangeable.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided constant-sharp minimax theorem identifying the leading constant and exhibiting a predictable allocation-estimator pair whose cumulative Neyman regret attains it.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves directly from oracle Neyman allocation to the learning cost of tracking unknown second moments.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: oracle Neyman allocation minimizes ATE variance -> sequential designs must learn arm second moments -> logarithmic regret is achievable -> what is the exact minimax constant?

method_exemplars.technique: Clipped second-moment tracking with a martingale and concentration proof for accumulated variance regret.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the attaining-design side for the same Neyman-regret functional, so sharpening its proof is the direct route to the upper constant.

method_exemplars.technique: Adaptive-experiment Le Cam testing through local alternatives and sequential likelihood-information control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower-bound machinery is structurally analogous to converting delayed learning of arm moments into an unavoidable adaptive estimation cost.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the minimax excess MSE over all non-anticipating designs and all measurable, possibly biased estimators satisfy R_n(s,r) ≥ c max{n^(-1-2s/(2s+d)), n^(-1-2r/(2r+d))} without any unbiasedness, regularity, or asymptotic-linearity restriction?

source_refs.claim: The finite-sample benchmark and second-order converse are stated for locally or exactly unbiased estimators, while the regular-estimator relaxation controls bias only at the first-order o(n^(-1/2)) scale.
source_refs.author: Jiachun Li and David Simchi-Levi

source_refs.claim: The paper develops a constrained-risk inequality that lower-bounds risk at one distribution from risk at another and applies to biased or superefficient estimators.
source_refs.author: John C. Duchi and Feng Ruan

open_problems.why_unsolved: Li and Simchi-Levi's second-order projection argument uses exact unbiasedness to turn excess variance into an L2 distance from an oracle statistic; after bias is allowed, that identity no longer lower-bounds excess MSE. Their o(n^(-1/2)) local-bias remark is first-order and permits bias much larger than the proposed n^(-1/2-s/(2s+d)) second-order scale. A valid converse must compare risks across nearby Hölder models while tracking the model-dependent subtraction V*(P)/n through the adaptive trajectory likelihood.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform two-point or fuzzy-hypothesis constrained-risk theorem for adaptive non-anticipating experiments proving the displayed lower bound for every measurable estimator, or a biased shrinkage estimator with a stated regime that falsifies it.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from average-propensity efficiency to a sharp second-order question is the setup to retain before pivoting from unbiased to unrestricted estimators.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: non-anticipating designs are summarized by average propensity -> generalized Neyman allocation gives the oracle first-order benchmark -> the second-order converse uses exact unbiasedness -> determine the excess-MSE frontier over every measurable estimator

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the Cauchy-Schwarz constrained-risk inequality to pairs or mixtures of adaptive-experiment laws instead of invoking an unbiased score-projection identity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The missing step is precisely a risk lower bound robust to bias and superefficiency.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the original constrained-risk construction for nonparametric functionals, using Hölder perturbations that change both the causal functional and oracle variance at controlled orders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical method for converting excellent risk at one model into unavoidable risk at a nearby model without estimator regularity.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a non-anticipating design and cross-fitted estimator attain R_n(s,r) ≤ C max{n^(-1-2s/(2s+d)), n^(-1-2r/(2r+d))} in mean-squared error with no logarithmic factor?

source_refs.claim: For linear outcome-mean functionals the paper gives a matching second-order rate only up to logarithmic factors and implements adaptation with a logarithmic number of batches.
source_refs.author: Jiachun Li and David Simchi-Levi

source_refs.claim: Clip-OGD obtains O(sqrt(T log T)) Neyman regret, illustrating a logarithmic loss in a related sequential allocation analysis.
source_refs.author: Jessica Dai, Paula Gradu, and Christopher Harshaw

open_problems.why_unsolved: The logarithms in current sequential constructions are entangled with geometric batching, simultaneous high-probability nuisance bounds, clipping and positivity control, and repeated policy updates. Fixed-design local-polynomial L2 risk bounds can be log-free, but inserting them into a predictable adaptive allocation without union-over-batches or time-uniform penalties requires a direct integrated-MSE analysis and a dependence-safe evaluation scheme.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit batched or continuously updated design-estimator pair, including sample splitting and nuisance learners, with a nonasymptotic expected-MSE upper bound at the displayed log-free rate.

writing_exemplar.why: The anchor already motivates operational batching and isolates two nuisance-driven second-order terms, so its narrative leads directly to log removal.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: the oracle propensity minimizes first-order variance -> the oracle must be learned sequentially from smooth nuisances -> batched cross-fitting reaches the benchmark up to logs -> construct a log-free attaining procedure

method_exemplars.technique: Use fold-specific history-measurable propensities and pooled cross-fitted scores so each nuisance estimate is independent of its evaluation observations, proving oracle equivalence in expectation rather than uniformly over update times.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete cross-fitting architecture for dependent batch-adaptive data and a pooled causal estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the U-statistic local-polynomial variance learner and integrated-risk calculation, which attain fixed-class minimax rates without a global union bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The design-relevant second moment is a heteroscedastic variance-type nuisance, and expected integrated risk enters excess MSE.

method_exemplars.technique: Use predictable A2IPW scores and a martingale decomposition to control causal estimation under sequentially learned propensities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly couples adaptive Neyman allocation with an influence-function estimator under sequential dependence.

open_problems.open_problem: For at most B policy updates, what is the minimax excess-MSE rate R_(n,B)(s,r), and what growth of B=B_n is necessary and sufficient to attain the unrestricted log-free frontier?

source_refs.claim: The attaining procedures use a logarithmic number of batches and present few policy updates as an operational advantage, but do not characterize the minimax price of a fixed update budget.
source_refs.author: Jiachun Li and David Simchi-Levi

source_refs.claim: Adaptive Neyman allocation is studied through a finite-stage competitive framework designed to work with a limited number of stages.
source_refs.author: Jinglong Zhao
source_refs.venue: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation

source_refs.claim: With a fixed small pilot, feasible Neyman allocation can have higher asymptotic variance than balanced randomization, with the loss depending on homoskedasticity and kurtosis.
source_refs.author: Yong Cai and Ahnaf Rafi

open_problems.why_unsolved: A fixed early pilot can leave allocation error non-negligible, whereas the anchor's geometric schedule repeatedly refreshes nuisance estimates and pays logarithmic bookkeeping. Existing finite-stage and small-pilot results are largely parametric or first-order and do not identify how Hölder outcome and variance errors propagate into excess MSE after each batch. Neither necessity of O(log n) updates nor sufficiency of fewer updates is known at the second-order scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower bounds for R_(n,B)(s,r) as a function of n, B, s, r, and d, including a threshold theorem for the smallest update budget attaining the full frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its operational case for batching provides the natural motivation, while its logarithmic schedule leaves the exact update-complexity tradeoff exposed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: fully reactive adaptation is operationally costly -> batching restores conditional i.i.d. structure -> logarithmically many batches attain the known second-order bound -> determine the minimal update budget and its statistical price

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the multistage competitive recursion that quantifies information gained early and allocation loss later.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the number of stages as a first-class constraint in Neyman allocation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the pooled cross-batch DML decomposition to expose each batch's propensity and nuisance error in the final estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired upper bound must exploit all batches rather than discard pilot observations.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize fixed-pilot alternative asymptotics and second-order delta-method calculations to nonparametric conditional variances and multiple updates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest witness that too little early information can make plug-in Neyman allocation inefficient.

open_problems.open_problem: Over the stated joint Hölder model, is the design-relevant conditional variance m_a(x)=ω_a(x)^2 σ_a(x)^2 learnable at the standalone exponent r/(2r+d), or does unknown rough μ_a force a slower joint (s,r,d)-dependent second-order excess-risk frontier?

source_refs.claim: The anchor expresses its sharp second-order rate through separate outcome-regression and conditional-second-moment nuisance rates.
source_refs.author: Jiachun Li and David Simchi-Levi

source_refs.claim: In random-design heteroscedastic regression, the minimax rate for estimating the variance function depends jointly and nontrivially on the smoothness of the unknown mean and variance.
source_refs.author: Yandi Shen, Chao Gao, Daniela Witten, and Fang Han

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that residuals from an optimal mean estimator can be suboptimal for variance-function estimation when the mean is rough.
source_refs.author: Lie Wang, Lawrence D. Brown, T. Tony Cai, and Michael Levine

open_problems.why_unsolved: In observed arm data, σ_a(x)^2 must be separated from an unknown μ_a(x), and random-design variance estimation can exhibit a joint smoothness bottleneck rather than the ordinary regression rate for a directly observed response. Sequential arm selection and inverse propensities further alter the effective design density. It is therefore not automatic that declaring σ_a(x)^2 Hölder makes its learnability exponent r/(2r+d); the proposed frontier may need another regime governed by variance-function estimation with unknown mean.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp L2 minimax theorem for estimating every m_a from adaptively assigned Gaussian arm data and the induced excess-risk frontier, or a paired-difference or U-statistic construction proving that the standalone exponent r/(2r+d) is valid.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation is precisely that unknown mean smoothness can change the variance-function minimax rate, the tension to resolve before adopting the conjectured variance exponent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: optimal allocation depends on conditional variances -> those variances are inferred from heteroscedastic regressions with unknown means -> variance estimation can have a joint mean-variance smoothness rate -> determine which exponent controls sequential causal excess risk

method_exemplars.technique: Port the U-statistic local-polynomial variance estimator and its matched mixture lower bound to propensity-weighted arm-specific random designs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly solves the analogous random-design variance problem with an unknown Hölder mean.

method_exemplars.technique: Use squared local differences to suppress mean bias and balance the two Hölder remainders in variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same bias mechanism arises when estimating design-relevant conditional variances from outcomes.

open_problems.open_problem: Does adaptive covariate balancing with a simple moment estimator have the same sharp log-free second-order excess-MSE frontier as regression-adjusted generalized-Neyman designs for linear causal functionals?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves a sharp second-order rate for the regression-adjustment route, while the balancing route attains the same first-order benchmark without an analogous sharp second-order characterization.
source_refs.author: Jiachun Li and David Simchi-Levi

source_refs.claim: Online balancing yields causal MSE bounds within a logarithmic factor of the best known offline design and leaves a conjectured online-discrepancy improvement.
source_refs.author: David Arbour, Drew Dimmery, Tung Mai, and Anup Rao

open_problems.why_unsolved: The balancing route replaces outcome-regression remainder control by an online discrepancy process while simultaneously learning a nonuniform covariate-dependent optimal allocation. Available online discrepancy bounds carry logarithmic losses and are usually stated for linear balance or worst-case finite-population outcomes, whereas this target is superpopulation excess MSE relative to a model-dependent semiparametric oracle. No result equates the balancing remainder with the Hölder nuisance terms at sharp order.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower second-order excess-MSE bounds for the balancing design and moment estimator, with an explicit regime comparison to regression adjustment and either removal or necessity of the online-discrepancy logarithm.

writing_exemplar.why: Its two-route organization naturally motivates asking whether benchmark equivalence extends from first order to the exact second-order frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: the oracle benchmark can be approached by estimator-side regression adjustment -> it can also be approached by assignment-side covariate balancing -> only the former has a sharp nuisance-rate refinement -> characterize and compare the balancing route at second order

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the weighted self-balancing walk, covariance Loewner bound, and implicit-ridge MSE comparison to learned generalized-Neyman probabilities and multiple arms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the online assignment construction and a causal MSE proof while exposing the logarithmic discrepancy loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine the anchor's batchwise balancing-remainder decomposition in expectation and match it against oracle-propensity learning error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already embeds balancing in the exact non-anticipating multi-arm semiparametric model of the desired theorem.

literature_map:
Li and Simchi-Levi (2026, arXiv:2606.31190) unify non-anticipating experiments through induced average propensity and give a second-order rate for linear causal functionals only up to logs.
Their lower-bound framework is locally or exactly unbiased; the regular relaxation controls only first-order o(n^(-1/2)) bias.
Armstrong (2022, arXiv:2205.02726) establishes broad first-order efficiency bounds for adaptive covariate-based experiments but no second-order unrestricted minimax theory.
Kato, Ishihara, Honda, and Narita (2020, arXiv:2002.05308) combine adaptive efficient allocation with A2IPW and martingale inference.
Li and Owen (2024, Journal of Causal Inference, arXiv:2309.15297) extend pooled cross-fitted DML to batch-adaptive designs.
Hahn, Hirano, and Karlan (2011, JBES) provide the foundational two-wave propensity-score design for minimizing the ATE efficiency bound.
Zhao (2024, EC, arXiv:2309.08808) treats limited-stage adaptive Neyman allocation through competitive analysis.
Dai, Gradu, and Harshaw (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2305.17187) obtain a sqrt(T log T) Neyman-regret bound, another sequential logarithmic loss.
Cai and Rafi (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2206.04643) show a fixed small pilot can make feasible Neyman allocation worse than balanced randomization.
Rafi (2023, arXiv:2305.08340) proves semiparametric efficiency for ATE estimation under covariate-adaptive randomization with fixed target proportions.
Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1902.10822) show variance-function minimax rates can depend jointly on mean and variance smoothness.
Wang, Brown, Cai, and Levine (2008, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0804.0709) show optimal mean residuals can be suboptimal for variance learning when the mean is rough.
Cai and Wang (2008, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0810.4780) obtain adaptive variance-function estimation with a logarithmic global-risk gap over inhomogeneous classes.
Brown and Low (1996) and Duchi and Ruan (2021, AISTATS, arXiv:1804.08116) provide constrained-risk tools for biased and superefficient estimators.
Arbour, Dimmery, Mai, and Rao (2022, arXiv:2203.02025) give online-balancing causal MSE bounds within a logarithmic factor of offline discrepancy designs.
